description: We’re a nimble team of engineers based in Boston, building FoodBuddy, a mobile app that helps people understand and track their nutritional intake. Through the NASA Space Apps Challenge, we want to push the boundaries of what our technology can do and explore a bigger question: Could FoodBuddy help astronauts monitor their nutrition during long-duration deep-space missions?
summary:
FoodBuddy Outer Space is an offline health-monitoring app designed for astronauts on long-duration space missions. It tracks eight health indicators: heart rate, blood pressure, oxygen saturation, respiratory rate, temperature, sleep, nutrition, and hydration.

Astronauts can record measurements using camera recognition, voice, or manual input, monitor trends, and receive health-check reminders. All data is stored locally, enabling operation without an internet connection.

The app addresses NASA’s challenge by helping astronauts independently collect and monitor health information. It also provides a foundation for future evidence-based health guidance, supporting astronaut well-being and mission readiness when medical assistance from Earth is limited.
details:
How It Works

The application brings eight health indicators into one dashboard: heart rate, blood pressure, oxygen saturation, respiratory rate, body temperature, sleep, nutrition, and hydration.

Astronauts can capture readings from medical-device displays using their phone’s camera, enter measurements manually or by voice, and record meals and fluid consumption. The application stores health records locally, displays historical trends, and provides reminders for routine health checks.

Technology

We developed the application using React Native, Expo, and TypeScript for iOS, with SQLite for offline data storage. Camera-based recognition and on-device AI support data capture without requiring cloud connectivity. The application is available for testing through Apple’s TestFlight on iOS 27.

Creativity and Benefits

Our approach combines physiological monitoring with nutrition and hydration tracking in a single mobile application. Instead of requiring astronauts to manually organize information from multiple medical instruments, FoodBuddy Outer Space provides a unified interface for recording and reviewing their health.

The team prioritized offline reliability, ease of use, minimal crew interaction, data privacy, and compatibility with existing medical equipment.

Intended Impact

FoodBuddy Outer Space aims to improve astronauts’ awareness of their health, reduce the effort required for routine monitoring, and support greater independence during missions beyond Earth.

The application also establishes a foundation for future evidence-based decision support using NASA research and authoritative clinical references, helping astronauts understand health changes and determine when further attention may be necessary.
